Live Updates: Iran says "ball is in the U.S. court" on deal to end war as Trump keeps his intentions veiled
Updated: November 2, 2026 / 12:45 PM EST (17:45 GMT). All entry times below are EST (GMT-5).

[~12:35 PM EST] Oil prices drop roughly 7% ahead of U.S. midterm elections
Oil prices fell approximately 7% as diplomatic signals between Tehran and Washington offered hope for resolving the Middle East conflict. Vice President JD Vance reportedly sent correspondence to Iranian national security official Mohsen Rezaei regarding potential talks—the highest-level outreach from the Trump administration in months.
Global Risk Management analyst Arne Lohmann Rasmussen stated: "may be tactical" ahead of elections, while warning that "attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz continue."
Brent crude declined 7.4% to $105.03 per barrel, with prices fluctuating between approximately $70 and $120 since the conflict began.

[~12:00 PM EST] Houthi spokesperson says Saudi coalition launched more than 100 strikes since Sunday
Brigadier General Yahya Saree announced: "Saudi warplanes launched 109 airstrikes over the past 24 hours," targeting Yemeni provinces including Saada, Taiz, Lahj, Al-Jawf, and Hodeidah.
Saree reported cumulative Saudi strikes totaling 3,939 since fighting escalated in autumn, and claimed Houthis conducted new attacks against Saudi infrastructure over the preceding 48 hours.

11:36 AM - Houthis claim new attacks on Saudi airport, military assets
Brigadier General Yahya Saree stated the group struck Dammam Airport "using two drones, and the operation achieved its objective successfully, resulting in the disruption of air traffic."
Additional reported strikes included an "early warning radar in Jizan" and "a military transport aircraft at Jizan Airport."

11:02 AM - Senior Iranian official thanks Putin, talks "strategic cooperation"
Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei discussed regional affairs and "strategic cooperation" with Russian President Vladimir Putin, with Rezaei thanking Putin for Russian support, according to Iran's Tasnim news agency.

10:28 AM - Iran's top diplomat says negotiations "proceeding very intensively"
Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated negotiations have been "proceeding very intensively" but "everything depends on" Washington's conduct. He warned: "If they intend to deceive us and launch military operations, they will face a response more bitter and forceful than before."

9:37 AM - Another tanker on fire near Strait of Hormuz
Iran's Navy claimed an unnamed oil tanker caught fire after striking a sea mine near the Strait's eastern entrance. The vessel had reportedly disabled navigation systems while attempting transit through shipping lanes Iran disputes.

8:58 AM - Iran says it proposed shorter 2-day implementation period
Foreign Minister Araghchi disclosed: "The Qatari side proposed shortening the implementation period...We have reached a proposal...that reduces the implementation period to two days."
Under this revised framework, "the Strait of Hormuz will reopen and maritime traffic will return to its previous conditions" on day two.

8:29 AM - Iran claims 11 tankers "caught fire" in 9 days
Iran's IRIB broadcaster reported 11 oil tankers caught fire since October 25, disputing U.S. Central Command Admiral Brad Cooper's characterization of strait routes as "free and clear."
The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations center separately documented 30 attacks on commercial vessels in October alone.

7:04 AM - Iran again warns of natural gas shortages ahead of winter
First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref urged public conservation, citing "imbalances accumulated over previous years and war-related damages," warning prices would increase for non-compliant consumers.

6:00 AM - Iran says the "ball is in the U.S. court"
Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei declared: "The ball is in the U.S. court, because our demands have been stated very clearly and transparently, and Iran's demands are reasonable and logical."
Negotiations centered on Iran's seven-day proposal from September, later shortened to two days.
(Search snippet language: "Three consecutive days of indirect, closed-door negotiations led by Qatar have yielded no apparent breakthrough, with Iran saying Monday that 'the ball is in the U.S. court.'")
